intent: The caption of a MenubarGroup or MenubarRadioGroup, shown above its items and used as the group's accessible name.
typical_uses: A section caption such as "Account" or "Sort by"

dont_use_when.situation: The caption of a form control outside a menu
A menu row the user can activate

invariants.text: Rendering the label outside a MenubarGroup or MenubarRadioGroup throws; the primitive looks up the group it labels from context.
The label renders `role="presentation"` and gives its id to the enclosing group's `aria-labelledby`; it is not focusable and is skipped by arrow-key navigation.

anti_patterns.dont: Style a MenubarItem with `disabled` to act as a caption
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use a MenubarLabel inside a group; a disabled item is still reached by arrow keys and announced as a menu item

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the label's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a label). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A caption over a sort choice

bad.title: A label straight under the popup
bad.why: There is no group for the label to name, so the primitive throws; wrap both in a MenubarGroup.
